about.label: About Me
about.heading: Research & Experience Strategy
about.p1: As a UX Designer and Researcher, my focus is on deeply understanding users before designing any solution. I firmly believe that the best digital experiences are born from rigorous research and continuous validation.
about.p2: My background as a Systems Analyst gives me a unique perspective: I can translate research insights into clear technical requirements, facilitating collaboration between design and development teams.
about.p3: I specialize in uncovering real user needs through interviews, usability testing, and data analysis, transforming those findings into optimized user flows and effective information architectures.
about.card1Text: Systems Analyst (final year). Structured approach to problem-solving, data analysis, and requirements documentation.
about.card2Text: Specialized in UX Research methodologies: interviews, usability testing, card sorting, heuristic analysis, and insight synthesis.

projects.label: Projects
projects.heading: Case studies
projects.intro: A selection of projects demonstrating my user research process, problem definition, and user-centered design solutions.

items.title: Personal Finance App
items.description: Comprehensive user research that revealed critical pain points, leading to a data-driven redesign that reduced the registration flow by 50%.
items.overview: This project consisted of deep user research to understand why the original app had a high drop-off rate. Through interviews, usability testing, and data analysis, we identified root problems and designed solutions validated with real users.
items.challenge: The original app had a 60% drop-off rate in the registration flow and users reported difficulty finding key features. The product team needed to understand the root causes before investing in development.
items.solution: I conducted mixed-methods research (qualitative and quantitative) that revealed information architecture problems and cognitive overload. Wireframes were iteratively validated with users before moving to high fidelity, ensuring solutions addressed real needs.

process.description: 12 in-depth user interviews, existing analytics analysis, benchmark of 5 competitors, and stakeholder mapping sessions.
Synthesis of 150+ insights through affinity mapping, creation of 3 data-driven personas, mapping of current and future state journey maps.
Co-creation workshop with users, new information architecture validated with card sorting (20 participants), iterative wireframes.
Usability testing with 8 participants (94% success rate vs 45% original), 3 iteration cycles based on findings.

results: Registration flow reduced from 6 to 3 steps (user-validated)
Critical task success rate increased from 45% to 94%
Information architecture reorganized based on card sorting with 20 users
Complete research documentation for future improvement cycles

items.title: E-learning Platform
items.description: Generative research with university students that informed the design of an educational platform with personalized learning paths.
items.overview: A generative research project to understand the needs and behaviors of university students in their online learning process, informing the design of a new platform from scratch.
items.challenge: Existing educational platforms had low student retention and high course abandonment. We needed to understand what motivated students and what barriers they faced in their learning experience.
items.solution: Through ethnographic research, diary studies, and in-depth interviews, we discovered that lack of personalization and immediate feedback were the main barriers. We designed an experience that adapts to individual learning styles.

process.description: 15 contextual interviews with students, 2-week diary study with 10 participants, benchmark of 6 platforms, and abandonment data analysis.
Affinity mapping of 200+ insights, 4 behavior-based personas, detailed experience maps, and key opportunity identification.
Co-design workshop with 8 students, tree testing of information architecture, iterative wireframes with validation at each cycle.
Remote usability tests with Maze (25 participants), heatmap analysis, 3 iteration cycles, and stakeholder findings presentation.

results: Identification of 4 distinct learning behavior patterns
Personalized path system based on research insights
Onboarding flow with 92% completion rate in testing
45-page research report for the product team

items.title: Management Dashboard
items.description: Internal user research and workflow analysis resulting in a modular dashboard with 40% task time reduction.
items.overview: Research focused on internal users of an organization to understand their current workflows and design a dashboard that centralizes metrics and tasks, improving operational efficiency.
items.challenge: The management team handled information across multiple disconnected tools, causing delays in decision-making and data duplication. We needed to understand real workflows before proposing solutions.
items.solution: I conducted contextual research observing users in their work environment, identifying pain points and automation opportunities. The modular design allows role-based customization, validated with each user group.

process.description: 6 shadowing sessions with users, interviews with 4 stakeholders, audit of existing tools, and critical task analysis.
Current workflow mapping, identification of 12 main pain points, prioritization with impact/effort matrix, and success metrics definition.
Card sorting to organize information by role, modular layout sketches with users, iterative wireframes with continuous feedback.
Usability testing with 6 end users, task time measurement, iterations, and usage pattern documentation.

results: 4 role-based customized views based on card sorting
Elimination of 3 redundant tools identified in research
UX metrics framework to measure post-launch adoption
